question: A 28-year-old woman in her first trimester presents with classic scabies. Her husband has similar itching. Which treatment plan is most appropriate?

answers.text: Permethrin 5% cream for both partners, applied overnight and repeated after 7 days, with bedding and clothing decontamination

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Permethrin 5% cream is the first-line scabicide and is safe in pregnancy and lactation. Both partners must be treated simultaneously — treating the index patient alone invites re-infestation from the symptomatic husband. Bedding and clothing worn in the preceding 48–72 hours should be washed at 60 °C or sealed for 72 hours.

answers.text: Oral ivermectin 200 mcg/kg single dose for the patient only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Ivermectin is best avoided in pregnancy owing to limited safety data. Additionally, treating only the patient would leave her husband as a source of re-infestation — all close contacts must be treated simultaneously on the same day.

answers.text: Lindane 1% lotion applied to the whole household

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Lindane carries a risk of neurotoxicity (seizures) and is avoided especially in pregnancy, infants, and young children. Permethrin 5% is the safe first-line choice with a far better safety profile.

answers.text: A potent topical corticosteroid until the pruritus settles

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Topical corticosteroids may relieve itch but do not kill the mite — the infestation will progress and spread. Treating the itch alone without eradicating the mite is one of the commonest causes of apparent 'treatment failure' in scabies.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: permethrin 5% is first-line and safe in pregnancy. Ivermectin is avoided in pregnancy. All close contacts must be treated simultaneously. Steroids address itch but not the infestation. A good treatment plan is always a household plan.

A complete scabies plan has four parts: the right scabicide (permethrin 5% — safe in pregnancy), simultaneous treatment of all contacts, environmental decontamination, and counselling that itch may persist 2–4 weeks after the mite is dead.
